So the receiver may get confused, may make mistakes. So, if the signal that we receive is sufficiently clean and strong, then it may be very close to the original one, and then the receiver may say, "Well, okay, this was definitely the signal here." And this means that, definitely, we are receiving zero zero one. But if the signal that we receive is very much deteriorated, and what we get is something here, then the receiver will say, "Well, the signal is likely this one." And then we can think of what we got is zero one zero, and make a mistake. So, the problem of having postulations with many signals is that they are more similar to each other, therefore the probability of mistaking one for another increases. That's the error probability in extracting the information bits from signals, and this probability increases.
